sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the Adriatic Sea just north of the city of Ancona and NW-ward offshore Pesaro. It is part of the Umbro-Marche Apennines outer offshore thrust. This front is the NE-verging fault system at the eastern border of the Northern Apennines chain, parallel to the Marche coast.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show only a sparse intermediate (4.5 < Mw < 5.0) seismicity.
The tectonic activity of this region is still not clearly documented but a plausible interpretation is that it is an offshore, shallower splay of the Northern Marche blind thrust. Subsurface data by Bally et al. (1986) have well imaged offshore anticlines to the southeast, whose growth would be caused by the NE-ward advancing thrust. Various evidence suggest that the region just onshore is undergoing NE-SW trending compression, including earthquake focal mechanisms all along the outer onshore front (Frepoli and Amato, 1997), while borehole breakout data (Montone et al., 2004) illustrated a NW-SE trending minimum stress axis.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped regional structures. The dip was based on subsurface data and geometrical considerations. The rake is assumed to represent pure thrusting, based on geological observations. The minimum and maximum depth were based on subsurface data and on geometrical considerations concerning the thrust geometry. The slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.

pictures.t: Cross-section through the northern Marche coastline
pictures.c: Eastern portion of a SW-NE cross-section Mt. Amiata-Perugia-Burano-Anna obtained by Bally et al. [1986] using seismic reflection data and well logs (from Bally et al. [1986]).

pictures.t: Model of active tectonic tilting for the central-northern Marche region [Vannoli et al., 2004]
pictures.c: Model of active tectonics in the northern Apennines frontal prism. Notice the rates of regional tilting inferred from the convergence of fluvial terraces and the fault slip rate inferred from the warping of the terraces (from Vannoli et al. [2004]).

The Stress Map of Italy shows a NE-SW compressional tectonic regime acting in the coastal Marche region. The directions of Shmin follow the trend of the Northern Apennines fronts from the southern Marche to the Po Plain (from Montone et al. [2004], modified).
